# Rank of $H_1$ of the Double Branched Cover of a Knot

## Setting Up the Problem

Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$, and let $\Sigma(K)$ denote its double branched cover. This is a closed, connected, orientable 3-manifold. The **rank** of $H_1(\Sigma(K);\,\mathbb{Z})$ means the rank of its free part, i.e., $\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(H_1(\Sigma(K))\otimes\mathbb{Q}\bigr)$.

## Key Theorem on Double Branched Covers

A classical result in 3-manifold topology states:

> For any knot $K \subset S^3$, the first homology group $H_1(\Sigma(K);\,\mathbb{Z})$ is a **finite** abelian group, with
> $$|H_1(\Sigma(K);\,\mathbb{Z})| = |\Delta_K(-1)|,$$
> where $\Delta_K(t)$ is the Alexander polynomial of $K$.

### Why $H_1$ is finite

The double branched cover $\Sigma(K)$ admits a Heegaard splitting whose handlebody presentation matrix (derived from the knot diagram) is a **square** matrix. This means the presentation of $H_1$ involves a square integer matrix $A$, and:

$$H_1(\Sigma(K)) \cong \mathbb{Z}^g / A\,\mathbb{Z}^g.$$

Since $A$ is $g\times g$, the quotient has finite order $|\det A|$ (if $\det A\neq 0$) or, more generally, the free rank is $g - \text{rank}(A) = 0$ because $A$ is square and its Smith normal form has no zero diagonal entries in the knot case. The determinant $|\det A| = |\Delta_K(-1)|$ is a positive integer, confirming $H_1$ is purely torsion.

## Verification with Examples

| Knot $K$ | $\Delta_K(t)$ | $\Delta_K(-1)$ | $H_1(\Sigma(K))$ | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unknot | $1$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| Trefoil | $-t+3-t^{-1}$ | $5$ → actually $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$... wait, trefoil gives Poincaré sphere | $0$ | $0$ |
| Figure-eight | $-t+3-t^{-1}$ | $5$ | $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ | $0$ |

In every case, $H_1$ is finite, so the free rank is zero.

## Conclusion

Since $H_1(\Sigma(K);\mathbb{Z})$ is a finite group for every knot $K\subset S^3$, it has no free part:

$$\text{rank}\; H_1(\Sigma(K);\mathbb{Z}) = 0.$$

$$\boxed{0}$$
